guide.title: WireGuard guide
guide.intro: WireGuard creates a private tunnel between your tower and your laptop. Here are the steps, using 10.0.0.1 for the tower and 10.0.0.2 for the laptop.
guide.step2: Create the WireGuard tunnel: for example 10.0.0.1 for the tower and 10.0.0.2 for the laptop, then bring it up on both sides.
guide.step3: On the tower: Lucania › Remote access, pick the WireGuard interface, keep port 4750, generate the key, then enable server mode.
guide.step3Firewall: Windows asks to allow Lucania through the firewall: accept for private networks, or create an inbound TCP 4750 rule limited to the WireGuard interface.
guide.step4: On the laptop: choose Remote mode, enter the address http://10.0.0.1:4750, paste the key, test the connection, then save.
guide.step5: The header dot follows the tower: gray when unreachable, orange with no model loaded, green when ready. Shutting the tower down uses Settings › Connections.
guide.security: Security: the connection uses plain HTTP, with no encryption of its own. Use it ONLY inside the WireGuard tunnel; the key only travels through that tunnel.
guide.docs: Full guide: docs/wireguard.md in the repository.

server.title: Share this machine (server mode)
server.description: This computer becomes a tower: it makes its engine available to another Lucania. The screen is then reserved for server mode until you stop it.

allowAll.warning: Listening on all interfaces exposes the engine to every network this computer is connected to, including the Internet if the port is open. Prefer the WireGuard interface.
